explanation_format: <repo discoveries and context> | <vendor description from Database-Description-AMOS-csv.csv>
grain: One row per (WP x department x sequence item x workstep x part request). WP header values repeat on every row. LEFT JOINs mean an item with no worksteps (or a step with no parts) still returns one row with NULLs in the missing columns.

repo: SESSION_CONTEXT.md (Key Technical Insights and Querying Rules)

encodings.date_int: Integer days since 1971-12-31. Convert in code (never in SQL output).
encodings.time_minutes: Integer minutes since midnight (CSV type TIME).
encodings.bool_yn: 'Y' / 'N' text flag; anything else is treated as false.

columns.explanation: Internal unique key of the workpack and the grouping key in code, because the WP row repeats once per department, item, step and part (1:N joins). | Internal unique-key of the Workpackage (counted with parameter 25)
Human-readable workpack name, unique per WP. Also the first ORDER BY column of this query. | Name of the Workpackage
Free-text description of the WP. Repeats on every row of the WP. | Description of the Workpackage
Station where the work is planned (e.g. HAN). Filter column of this query (currently hardcoded to 'HAN'; it is meant to be a parameter). | Station for that the work is planned
Aircraft registration of the WP. The query header says it is parameterized by ac_registr, but the WHERE clause does not filter on it yet. | Aircraft-Registry of the affected A/C

Department responsible for / handed the WP. Multi-valued: a WP can have several departments and the join repeats the WP row once per department (group by z_WP_ID in code). Filtered to 'NTHN' in this query, so only that department's rows come back. | Department code responsible for the WP. Foreign key to the department table.

Present-day (real-time) status of the WP via wp_header.wp_status, a N:1 lookup to wp_status. The query filters on 'In Progress', 'Issued' and 'Closed'. Do NOT use it to reconstruct historical activity; use the date columns instead. | Name of the Workpackage status

columns.alias_status: none yet (proposed name: wp_status_closed). Selected as the raw column name, so the CSV header is 'closed'.
columns.explanation: Whether the status counts as closed (Y/N). Decode to boolean in code. The query's own filter uses the status name ('Closed'), not this flag. | Indicates whether the status is considered closed ('Y' for yes, 'N' for no)

Scheduled start date as an AMOS integer. Used by Condition 1 (In Progress / Issued WPs that started within the last 6 months): DATE '1971-12-31' + start_date. | Scheduled start date as number of days since 31.Dec.1971

Scheduled start time as minutes since midnight (a TIME column, not milliseconds). Combine with z_WP_START_DATE in code to get a real timestamp (derived field wp_start). | Scheduled Start-Time in minutes since day begin

WARNING: when a WP is closed, AMOS does not populate act_end_date / act_end_time, only wp_header.end_date. Expect NULL here, including for Closed WPs. The query's closed-WP filter uses wp_header.end_date / end_time, which are not selected. | Real end-date
Same caveat as z_WP_ACT_END_DATE: usually NULL for closed WPs. Minutes since midnight when present. | Real end-time

1st level of the WP item number (item '3.23' has 1st = 3). Together with z_WP_SEQ_2ND it identifies the WP item; wp_sequence links the WP to every event in wo_header (work orders, templates, pendings, jobcards, etc.). | Prefix for the sequence number, corresponding to the event type or check. For example, if the sequence number is '3.342', this column contains '3'.

2nd level of the WP item number (item '3.23' has 2nd = 23). Watch for negative values: they mark duplicate sequences, so check before treating (1st, 2nd) as a unique key. | The sequence number, starting at 1 for each WP. A negative value indicates a duplicate sequence; the original value is stored in the deprecated old_seqno_i column.

3rd level of the sequence: orders the worksteps inside one WP item (item 3.23, step 1, step 2, ...). NULL when the item has no worksteps (LEFT JOIN). It is the last ORDER BY column. | Step's position in the sequence of steps within the Work Template.

Status of the WP item's underlying wo_header record (O = Open, C = Closed). wo_header is a universal container (work orders, work templates, event pendings, jobcards, shopcards), so this also applies to non-WO items. | State of a WO: O = Open WO C = Closed WO

Title/name of the WP item, found by probing. Use wo_event_link (1:1 with wo_header), NOT wp_history, which is an append-only log and multiplies rows (1:N). | Name of the Maintenance Event. It will be used to globally improve the performance of the Maintenance Event framework without using the associated Maintenance Requirements.

Longer display variant of the item title (up to 300 characters vs 100 for event_name). Compare against z_WP_IT_NAME to see which one holds the title you want. | Display of the Maintenance Event. It will be used to globally improve the performance of the Maintenance Event framework without using the associated Maintenance Requirements.

Step title / summary. Always select header, text and text_html together to get the full step text, because only one of text / text_html is filled. NULL when the item has no steps. | Header description of the work step.

Plain-text step body. Only populated when the step was saved as plain text; formatted steps leave it NULL and use z_WP_IT_TEXT_HTML. Can contain newlines and commas, so use proper CSV quoting. | Plain description or work step text. This field is only populated if the text was saved as plain text; otherwise, it is empty (NULL).

Formatted (HTML) step body. This is where formatted step descriptions are stored; NULL for plain-text steps. Can be very large; strip or sanitize the HTML in code. | Formatted description or work step text. This field is only populated if the text was saved as formatted; otherwise, it is empty (NULL).

Part number required to perform the step (down to workstep level). Joined by part_request_2.event_key = workstep_link.workstep_linkno_i AND event_type = 'WSL'. A step with N part requests returns N rows (the step text repeats); NULL when the step needs no parts. | The requested P/N.

Required quantity of z_PART_NO for that workstep. Floating point (float8), so it may be fractional. The related percentage column (qty reduced after each use) is not selected. | The requested quantity of the part.
Y = the part number is not in the forecast and needs attention (flag these in validation). | 'Y' if the part request must not appear in the Parts Consumption Forecast.
